Artemis II (2026-04-01) · first crewed lunar flyby since Apollo 17, 1972

The crew vehicle for NASA’s Artemis program, built jointly with ESA (the European Service Module is provided by Airbus). Designed to support up to four astronauts on multi-week missions to lunar orbit. Flew uncrewed on Artemis I in 2022. Flew its first crewed mission (Artemis II) in April 2026 with a four-person crew on a lunar flyby trajectory.
First crewed flight beyond low-Earth orbit since Apollo 17 (1972) — and the mission that inspired this project
First crewed test of the commercial lunar landers — Orion plans to dock with one or both in Earth orbit
First crewed lunar landing since Apollo 17 (1972)
Second crewed landing of the Artemis era — the start of a lunar base
Heavy lift for Artemis lunar program
Apollo 10 + Skylab + 53 Shuttle flights; now NASA's SLS / Artemis pad
OV-105 — fifth Shuttle, built from spares to replace Challenger. First Hubble servicing STS-61 (1993); delivered Unity + Canadarm2
OV-104 — fourth Shuttle. Flew final mission STS-135 (2011), final Hubble servicing STS-125 (2009), deployed Galileo + Magellan
OV-103 — third Shuttle. Deployed Hubble (STS-31, 1990); flew both return-to-flight missions. 39 missions — most of any orbiter
OV-099 — second operational Shuttle. Lost 73s after launch on STS-51-L (1986-01-28) with all seven crew including teacher Christa McAuliffe
OV-102 — the first Shuttle orbiter to fly to space (STS-1, 1981-04-12); lost on re-entry STS-107 2003-02-01

Planned as the first crewed lunar landing since Apollo 17 in 1972 — a gap of more than 55 years, and the first ever near the south pole. The target is the water ice in permanently shadowed craters, which may one day supply drinking water, oxygen and rocket propellant. Artemis IV took this role in 2026, when NASA turned Artemis III into an Earth-orbit test; it is planned for early 2028.
